body: Adrastea, inner moon of Jupiter, distinct from Metis, Amalthea and Thebe
status: Research-only native preparation; no dossier92, embedding, catalogue, map, model, shape or codec adoption.

products.identity: Whole portrait, left to right: Metis, Adrastea, Amalthea, Thebe. Adrastea is the tiny second disk from left. Target metadata lists Amalthea; caption explicitly covers all four moons, so retain the scope distinction. No other moon supplies Adrastea geography.

publisherStatements.orientation: North approximately up; correct relative sizes.

products.inspection: Whole856x270 one-channel JPEG inspected. Adrastea is a tiny blurred bright disk; sampled brightness does not establish local rocks, grains, chemistry, calibrated visible colour, a registered complete globe or absence of atmosphere. Other disks and bright patches are separate bodies. No angular/raster computation.

Historical first-resolved wording is not a current best/latest-image claim.
